ColonyCouncil.WorldSituationDef.label: a raid on a town the colony was

texts.li: [runner,!nohead] A runner from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the way to the colony with word from {OTHER_nameDef}: a war band of {ENEMY} is camped in the woods above the town, and more of them come in every night.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once. Its people mean to keep it.

[runner,nohead] A runner from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the way to the colony: a war band of {ENEMY} is camped above the town, and its people are piling stones in the gaps of the old fence.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once. Its people mean to keep it.

[rider,!nohead] A rider is coming hard from {PLACE}, {TALE}, with word from the {TITLE}, {OTHER_nameDef}: raiders of {ENEMY} are on the roads around the town, and it has shut its gates.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and the hall the colony built is its keep now.

[rider,nohead] A rider is coming hard from {PLACE}, {TALE}: raiders of {ENEMY} are on the roads around the town, and it has shut its gates.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and the hall the colony built is its keep now.

[radio,!nohead] The radio carries a call from {PLACE}, {TALE}: {OTHER_nameDef}, its {TITLE}, says raiders of {ENEMY} are gathering outside the town in trucks and on foot.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and its walls are the colony's walls.

[radio,nohead] The radio carries a call from {PLACE}, {TALE}: raiders of {ENEMY} are gathering outside the town in trucks and on foot.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and its walls are the colony's walls.

[comms,!nohead] A comms call from {PLACE}, {TALE}: {OTHER_nameDef}, its {TITLE}, reports a strike group of {ENEMY} closing on the settlement.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once. Its defences are the ones the colony built.
[comms,nohead] A comms call from {PLACE}, {TALE}: a strike group of {ENEMY} is closing on the settlement.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once. Its defences are the ones the colony built.

[runner,!nohead] A runner from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is coming with word from {OTHER_nameDef}: {ENEMY} have been seen around the town, and its people have brought everyone in behind the old walls.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and it is calling on the colony now.

[runner,nohead] A runner from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is coming to the colony: {ENEMY} have been seen around the town, and its people have brought everyone in behind the old walls.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and it is calling on the colony now.

[rider,!nohead] A rider from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the road with a sealed message from the {TITLE}, {OTHER_nameDef}: a band of {ENEMY} is moving against the town.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and its gates are the ones the colony hung.
[rider,nohead] A rider from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the road to the colony: a band of {ENEMY} is moving against the town.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and its gates are the ones the colony hung.
[radio,!nohead] {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the radio: {OTHER_nameDef}, its {TITLE}, is calling every friend the town has, and the colony first, because {ENEMY} are coming.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once.
[radio,nohead] {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the radio, calling every friend the town has, and the colony first, because {ENEMY} are coming.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once.

[comms,!nohead] {PLACE}, {TALE}, has opened a channel to the colony: {OTHER_nameDef}, its {TITLE}, has a raid force of {ENEMY} on the long-range scans.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and it still runs on the colony's systems.

[comms,nohead] {PLACE}, {TALE}, has opened a channel to the colony: a raid force of {ENEMY} is on the settlement's long-range scans.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and it still runs on the colony's systems.

[runner,enemyEmpire] A runner from {PLACE}, {TALE}, is on the way to the colony: soldiers of {ENEMY}, the Empire's own, have come against the town, and its people have shut themselves in.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once. Its people mean to keep it.

[rider,enemyEmpire] A rider is coming hard from {PLACE}, {TALE}: an imperial company of {ENEMY} is on the roads around the town, and it has barred its gates.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and it will not bow to them without a fight.

[radio,enemyEmpire] The radio carries a call from {PLACE}, {TALE}: troops of {ENEMY} under the Empire's banners are closing on the town.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once, and its walls are the colony's walls.

[comms,enemyEmpire] A comms call from {PLACE}, {TALE}: an imperial strike force of {ENEMY} is closing on the settlement in good order.\n\n{PLACE} was the colony once. Its defences are the ones the colony built.

summaries.li: {PLACE} holds its gate against {ENEMY} as long as it can. Fighters the colony sends by caravan are waited for, and fight on the town's own ground.

texts.li: [runner,!nohead] {OTHER_nameDef}'s runner is at the colony, out of breath: {PLACE} is holding its fence against {ENEMY}, and asks whether the colony it was will send fighters.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.

[runner,nohead] A runner from {PLACE} is at the colony, out of breath: the town is holding its fence against {ENEMY}, and asks whether the colony it was will send fighters.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.

[rider,!nohead] The rider from {PLACE} brings the {TITLE}'s own words: {OTHER_nameDef} asks the colony to send fighters against {ENEMY}, for the sake of the town it was.\n\nThe town will hold its gates as long as it can.
[rider,nohead] The rider from {PLACE} asks the colony to send fighters against {ENEMY}, for the sake of the town it was.\n\nThe town will hold its gates as long as it can.

[radio,!nohead] {OTHER_nameDef} comes back on the radio: {PLACE} can hold its walls against {ENEMY} for a while, and asks whether the colony will send fighters.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.
[radio,nohead] The radio again: {PLACE} can hold its walls against {ENEMY} for a while, and asks whether the colony will send fighters.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.

[comms,!nohead] {OTHER_nameDef} asks over comms for a strike team from the colony: {PLACE}'s defences can hold {ENEMY} off for a while, not for good.\n\nThe settlement will hold out as long as it can.
[comms,nohead] The call from {PLACE} asks for a strike team from the colony: its defences can hold {ENEMY} off for a while, not for good.\n\nThe settlement will hold out as long as it can.

[runner,!nohead] The runner from {PLACE} has reached the colony's gate with {OTHER_nameDef}'s words: {ENEMY} are at the town, and it asks for the colony's fighters to stand with it.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.
[runner,nohead] The runner from {PLACE} has reached the colony's gate: {ENEMY} are at the town, and it asks for the colony's fighters to stand with it.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.

[rider,!nohead] The rider from {PLACE} has come to the colony's gate: the {TITLE}, {OTHER_nameDef}, asks for fighters to hold the town against {ENEMY}.\n\nThe town will hold its gates as long as it can.
[rider,nohead] The rider from {PLACE} has come to the colony's gate to ask for fighters to hold the town against {ENEMY}.\n\nThe town will hold its gates as long as it can.
[radio,!nohead] {OTHER_nameDef} is on the radio from {PLACE} again: {ENEMY} are at the walls, and the town asks whether the colony will send fighters.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.
[radio,nohead] {PLACE} is on the radio again: {ENEMY} are at the walls, and the town asks whether the colony will send fighters.\n\nThe town will hold out as long as it can.

[comms,!nohead] A second call from {PLACE}: {OTHER_nameDef} requests a strike team from the colony against {ENEMY}, while the settlement's defences still hold.\n\nThe settlement will hold out as long as it can.
[comms,nohead] A second call from {PLACE} requests a strike team from the colony against {ENEMY}, while the settlement's defences still hold.\n\nThe settlement will hold out as long as it can.

li.label: Send fighters to {PLACE}
li.outcome: {PLACE} will hold out for the colony's fighters. Form their caravan for the town: two grown colonists or more, by caravan, or by pods or shuttle where the colony has them.

li.label: Send word that the colony cannot come
li.outcome: {PLACE} has the colony's answer, and readies itself alone.

outcomes.li: [runner] The runner sets off back to {PLACE} with the colony's answer.
[rider] The rider turns for {PLACE} with the colony's answer.
[radio] The colony answers over the radio that it cannot come. {PLACE} readies itself alone.
[comms] The colony answers over comms that it cannot come. {PLACE} readies itself alone.
[runner] The runner takes the colony's answer back to {PLACE}, where its people are making ready without it.
[rider] The rider heads back to {PLACE} with the colony's no, and the town makes ready on its own.
[radio] The colony's answer goes back over the radio: it cannot send anyone. {PLACE} will hold alone.
[comms] The colony replies that it has nobody to spare. {PLACE} closes the channel and readies its defences.

texts.li: [!died] The raiders of {ENEMY} are gone from {PLACE}. The colony's fighters stood on the old walls beside the town's own people, and the town has not forgotten whose walls they were.\n\n{FACTION} will remember it.

[died] The raiders of {ENEMY} are gone from {PLACE}, but not without a price: {DEAD}, one of the colony's own once, fell beside the colony's fighters.\n\n{FACTION} will remember who came when they called.
[!died] {PLACE} stands. The raiders of {ENEMY} are dead or fled, and the colony's fighters can rest inside the walls the colony built.\n\n{FACTION} will remember who came.
[!died,theirLowtech] {ENEMY} are beaten at {PLACE}, and the town's people and the colony's fought them side by side at the old walls.\n\n{FACTION} will tell of it at their fire for a long time.
[died,!diedMany] {PLACE} stands, and {ENEMY} are beaten. {DEAD}, who stayed at {PLACE} when it was handed over, did not live to see it.\n\n{FACTION} will remember who came when they called.

[died,diedMany] The raiders of {ENEMY} are gone from {PLACE}, at a hard price: {DEAD}, who were the colony's own once, fell beside the colony's fighters.\n\n{FACTION} will remember who came when they called.
[!died] The raiders of {ENEMY} broke into {PLACE} while the colony's fighters were still in the fight, and took what they could. The town still stands, poorer than it was.

[died] The raiders of {ENEMY} broke into {PLACE} while the colony's fighters were still in the fight, and took what they could. {DEAD}, one of the colony's own once, died in the fight.\n\nThe town still stands, poorer than it was.

[!died] {ENEMY} forced their way into {PLACE} before the fight was done, and carried off what they could. The colony's fighters did all they could to stop them.\n\nThe town still stands, poorer than it was.
[died,!diedMany] {ENEMY} forced their way into {PLACE}, and {DEAD}, once one of the colony's own, was killed in the fighting.\n\nThe town still stands, poorer than it was.

[died,diedMany] {ENEMY} forced their way into {PLACE} while the colony's fighters were still in the fight. {DEAD}, all of them the colony's own once, were killed.\n\nThe town still stands, poorer than it was.
[refused] {PLACE} held without the colony. {ENEMY} tried the walls for a night and a day and went off after easier towns.\n\nIts people are tired, and short of a little of everything.
[nobodyCame] The colony's fighters never came, but {PLACE} held. {ENEMY} tried the walls and went off after easier towns.\n\nIts people waited for the colony, and noticed when it did not come.
[seen] The colony's fighters left before the end, and {PLACE} held without them. {ENEMY} have gone off after easier towns.
[!refused,!nobodyCame,!seen] {PLACE} held. {ENEMY} tried the walls and went off after easier towns.
[refused] {PLACE} held on its own. {ENEMY} could not get over the old walls and went looking elsewhere.\n\nIts people know the colony said no, and they managed without it.
[nobodyCame] {PLACE} waited for the colony's fighters and held without them. {ENEMY} have gone.\n\nThe town is tired, and it noticed who did not come.
[seen,!died] {PLACE} held after the colony's fighters had left. {ENEMY} gave up on its walls in the end.
[seen,died,!diedMany] The colony's fighters left before the end, and {PLACE} held without them, but {DEAD}, once one of the colony's own, was killed in the fighting.
[seen,died,diedMany] The colony's fighters left before the end, and {PLACE} held without them, but {DEAD}, all of them the colony's own once, were killed in the fighting.
[!refused,!nobodyCame,!seen] {ENEMY} gave up on {PLACE} in the end, and the town is still its own.
[!died,!others] {ENEMY} were beaten back at the gate of {PLACE}, but not before they burned its outer fields and took what they found there. The town has lost goods and fortune.
[!died,others] {ENEMY} were beaten back at the gate of {PLACE}, but not before they burned its outer fields. Among the town's dead is {ITEM}.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[died,!others] {ENEMY} were beaten back at the gate of {PLACE}. {DEAD}, one of the colony's own once, was killed holding it.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[died,others] {ENEMY} were beaten back at the gate of {PLACE}. {DEAD}, one of the colony's own once, was killed holding it, and so was {ITEM}.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[!died,!others] {PLACE} drove {ENEMY} off, at a cost: stores lost, fields trampled and a long clearing-up ahead.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[!died,others] {PLACE} drove {ENEMY} off, but {ITEM} did not live to see it.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[died,!diedMany,!others] {PLACE} drove {ENEMY} off, but {DEAD}, who stayed there when it was handed over, was killed at the gate.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[died,diedMany,!others] {ENEMY} were beaten back at the gate of {PLACE}. {DEAD}, all of them the colony's own once, were killed holding it.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.

[died,diedMany,others] {ENEMY} were beaten back at the gate of {PLACE}. {DEAD}, all of them the colony's own once, were killed holding it, with {ITEM} beside them.\n\nThe town has lost goods and fortune.
[!died,!others] {ENEMY} broke into {PLACE} and took most of what it had. The town still stands, but it will be a long time before it stands as it did.
[!died,others] {ENEMY} broke into {PLACE} and took most of what it had. Among the town's dead is {ITEM}.\n\nThe town still stands, but it will be a long time before it stands as it did.

[died,!others] {ENEMY} broke into {PLACE} and took most of what it had. {DEAD}, one of the colony's own once, was killed in the raid.\n\nThe town still stands, but it will be a long time before it stands as it did.

[died,others] {ENEMY} broke into {PLACE} and took most of what it had. {DEAD}, one of the colony's own once, was killed in the raid, and so was {ITEM}.\n\nThe town still stands, but it will be a long time before it stands as it did.
[!died,!others] {PLACE} was sacked by {ENEMY}. Its people are still there, picking through what was left.\n\nIt will be a long time before the town stands as it did.
[!died,others] {ENEMY} sacked {PLACE}, and {ITEM} died in the raid.\n\nThe town still stands, but it will be a long time before it stands as it did.
[died,!others] {ENEMY} sacked {PLACE}. {DEAD}, who stayed there when it was handed over, is among the dead.\n\nThe town still stands, but it will be a long time before it stands as it did.
Word from {PLACE} has stopped. Whatever came of the raid, the town is not what it was when it called the colony.
The raid on {PLACE} is no longer the colony's to answer: the town is not what it was when it called.
